# Jarvis Registry

> Jarvis Registry is a self-hostable enterprise gateway and registry for governed access to MCP servers, A2A agents, and private AI skills.

Last updated: 2026-10-30T18:46:04Z

Use the guides below for deployment, developer clients, business chatbot integrations, identity, access control, and operations. Capabilities depend on deployment configuration and the connected platform. Private deployment does not itself confer compliance certification.

- [Documentation](https://jarvisregistry.com/)
- [Source repository](https://github.com/ascending-llc/jarvis-registry)
- [Full documentation text](https://jarvisregistry.com/llms-full.txt)

## Overview

- [Jarvis Registry](https://jarvisregistry.com/): Jarvis Registry is a self-hostable enterprise AI gateway and registry for connecting AI clients to governed MCP servers(tools), agents, and private skills. Deploy it in your environment and use its identity, access-control, and...
- [Why use Registry](https://jarvisregistry.com/FEATURES/): Jarvis Registry is the enterprise control plane for AI — connecting copilots, autonomous agents, and enterprise tools through a single, secure, and observable gateway. It handles both MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and A2A agents...

## Get Started

- [Quick Start](https://jarvisregistry.com/quick-start/): Get the Jarvis Registry running in 5 minutes with this streamlined setup guide.
- [Generate Secrets](https://jarvisregistry.com/generate-secrets/): All keys are generated locally in your browser using the Web Crypto API . Nothing is sent to any server.
- [Production Deployment: Overview](https://jarvisregistry.com/deployment-guide/): This guide is cloud-platform-agnostic. It describes what components are needed and why for deploying Jarvis Registry to an existing Kubernetes cluster on AWS (EKS) or Azure (AKS). Sections that differ between platforms are clearly marked.
- [Production Deployment: Configuration](https://jarvisregistry.com/production-configuration/): Choose the instructions for your role: developers connect local IDE to the centralized MCP gateway; organization administrators make it available in business chatbots such as Claude and ChatGPT; deployment operators configure the...

## Core Features

- [IDP Integration](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/auth-server/): Jarvis Registry ships with a built-in Auth Server — a standards-compliant OpenID Connect (OIDC) and OAuth 2.0 authorization server. It handles token issuance, validation, and refresh for all users and AI agents connecting to the gateway.
- [MCPServer Gateway & Registry](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/mcp-gateway-registry/): Jarvis Registry's MCP Gateway is a single authenticated entry point for MCP-compatible clients to discover and invoke registered Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The MCP Registry catalogs those servers and their metadata;...
- [A2AAgent Gateway & Registry](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/a2a-gateway-registry/): The A2A Agent Gateway & Registry is the central catalog for autonomous agents exposed through Jarvis Registry. It lets platform teams register agents, organize them by skills and capabilities, control who can access them, and expose...
- [Skill Gateway](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/skill-gateway/): The Skill Gateway is a private, organization-managed catalog for authoring, importing, governing, and distributing approved AI skills. Skills remain private by default and are shared through Registry ACLs; the AI Skills CLI delivers...
- [AI Skills CLI](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/ai-skills-cli/): The Jarvis Registry CLI delivers accessible private Registry skills into local developer environments. It lets developers consume organization-approved skills without manually copying content or handling Registry credentials in scripts....
- [AWS AgentCore Federation](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/agentcore-federation/): AgentCore Federation connects an external Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway to Jarvis Registry so platform admins can import and govern resources from one control plane.
- [Azure AI Foundry Federation](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/foundry-ai-federation/): Azure AI Foundry Federation connects an external Azure AI Foundry workspace to Jarvis Registry so platform admins can import and govern agents from one control plane.
- [Workflow Orchestration](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/workflow-orchestration/): Jarvis Registry workflow orchestration lets you compose A2A agents, MCP tools, and skills into multi-step pipelines that complete complex tasks — with conditional logic, parallel execution, and human approval gates.
- [Registry Endpoint](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/registry-endpoint/): The Registry Endpoint is the single MCP entry point that AI copilots use to access your enterprise tools and agents.
- [Observability](https://jarvisregistry.com/features/observability/): Jarvis instruments every layer of the platform with OpenTelemetry and ships that telemetry through a vendor-neutral pipeline. The goal is simple: connect to whatever observability backend you already use — Grafana, New Relic, Datadog,...

## Walkthroughs

- [Test MCP Access with Two Users](https://jarvisregistry.com/walkthroughs/mcp-access-control/): Before connecting a business system, check whether your Jarvis Registry deployment stops an unauthorized user from calling a registered MCP server, even when that user knows its server ID and tool name. This walkthrough uses two...
- [Private Skill Import, Updates & Access Removal](https://jarvisregistry.com/walkthroughs/private-skill-lifecycle/): Use this walkthrough to check how a private GitHub skill moves into Jarvis Registry, reaches an authorized developer, receives an update, and is removed from the CLI's managed directory after access is revoked.

## Architecture & Design

- [Security Control Design](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/security-design/): Security in the registry is layered. Each layer has a distinct responsibility, and they compose in a fixed order on every request. This design aligns with enterprise AI governance best practices and the Jarvis AI Guardrails model for...
- [RBAC & Scopes](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/scopes/): The registry uses a two-layer authorization model: scopes control which API endpoints a user can call, and ACL controls which specific resources they can see or modify within those endpoints. This model is grounded in enterprise AI...
- [ACL Connector Service](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/acl-connector-service/): Introduction
- [A2A Agent API](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/a2a-agent-api-design/): All agent responses follow this structure:
- [Agent Workflow](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/agent-workflow/): Architecture: Agno as outer workflow runtime (operator controls, pause/resume, SSE streaming) + PydanticAI as internal protocol executor (MCP tool calls, A2A agent handoffs). Customer-facing schema is pure Pydantic — no runtime...
- [AgentCore Integration](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/agentcore/): This guide demonstrates how to register and use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway as an MCP server through the MCP Gateway Registry.
- [Federation Guide](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/federation/): The MCP Gateway Registry supports federation with external registries, allowing you to import and manage servers/agents from multiple sources through a unified interface.
- [Federation API](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/federation-api/): Base URL: /api/v1
- [DB Persistence](https://jarvisregistry.com/design/mcp_db_persistence_design/): Living design document for MongoDB integration
